cells.tense: Right now you can sit with someone else's feeling and still know where you end.
cells.ask: Offer to sit with one person this week, and while you're there keep track of where their feeling stops and yours starts.
cells.core:
The room isn't dark and it isn't lit. You've got enough to see the next few steps and not the shape of the whole thing, and you're not standing around waiting for the rest to arrive. You move when the next stretch shows itself, and you let the rest stay unknown.

That's how it works with people too. Someone brings you something half-finished -- a story they can't end, a mood they can't name -- and you don't rush them into a shape. You stay close, and you stay yourself. You're not pretending to feel it with them, and you're not backing off into politeness either. Something in you stays put while their feeling moves, and they can feel the difference. Keep a little of that steadiness in reserve when the week gets loud.
cells.sheetLine: You sit with it and stay yourself. That's the whole thing.
cells.verb: feeling with people and staying distinct
cells.place: in the middle of not knowing how it goes

cells.tense: You're already living in how it will feel when this goes wrong for someone you care about.
cells.ask: When you catch yourself rehearsing someone's pain tonight, write down what's actually happening now, and let one thing end because it already has.
cells.core:
Before anything has happened, you're already in it -- you can feel how bad it's going to be for them, how it will land, what you'll have to hold. The future is crowded and no one has arrived there yet. You meet people from inside that rehearsal, and they can feel you somewhere else.

You're not indifferent. You're too far in. You take on a friend's unexplained silence as if it were written to you, and by the time they speak you've already carried the whole ending. That's not steadiness; that's being everywhere at once. Sometimes something is genuinely over and you keep it open because closing it feels cruel -- the story stays alive on fumes. What ends was real and already ending. Let the thing that has finished actually finish, then see how much of it is still yours to feel.
cells.sheetLine: You keep carrying endings that haven't happened yet.

cells.tense: You went quiet in order to keep the peace, and you're still standing at that door.
cells.ask: Tell one person one true thing about how you're doing, and stop there. No follow-up questions, no fixing, just say it and let it sit.
cells.core:
Conversations run smoothly and nothing reaches you. You know how to be warm enough that no one asks -- you keep your side light and you don't lean in, and that's been a way of getting through. You're still doing it now. The people around you get the surface and you get the surface too, and nobody says anything about it.

You can't order feeling back, and you can't force your way to caring. What you can do is get steady again -- not by feeling more, but by feeling straight. That means knowing what's actually yours in a room, what's theirs, what you're carrying by accident. Tell one person one true thing about how your day went, no performance, no summarising. Say it and let them do what they do with it. Your side of the room gets a little more solid just by being occupied out loud.
cells.sheetLine: You kept the peace by leaving the room. You can come back.

cells.tense: You're steady with people in a way others notice, and you treat it as just being sensible.
cells.ask: Name one thing you did this week that held someone steady, and call it care instead of getting it done.
cells.core:
Someone's had a rough day, and you check in before you've thought about it. You lift the weight off them without being asked, you stay in the room when leaving would be easier. Anyone close to you could describe this about you faster than you could.

That's the part you keep stepping past -- not out of cruelty, but because you've decided that's not a thing you do, feelings being shaky ground and all. You file it under practical, reliable, easy to have around. Those are real. They're just the outside of something else you haven't named. You don't have to start feeling more to make it true. Notice one instance where you showed up for someone, and say out loud that it was care.
cells.sheetLine: People already feel it. You've not once said it's yours.
